claim: The two orders of gods are one species, and it calls itself Zenar; the other faction is Zenad
where_in_game: 81 copies in 45 places, the Balmora bookseller among them
note: The one record that teaches the distinction. Frozen against the rules: explaining a word and replacing it everywhere are opposite operations.

claim: Kinship is a decision, not a property: the Temple goes on saying Daedra because not-kin may be used as one likes
carrier: the book; Caius Cosades, topic Blades; Gilvas Barelo, topic Zenar
where_in_game: Balmora, from the first main-quest conversation

claim: They call themselves Zenar. Two words exist for one thing, and which you use says who is doing the calling
carrier: Caius Cosades, topics little advice and Blades
note: Satisfies Morrowind Part 5's placement requirement: the two vocabularies must be legible early or the mod reads as broken.

claim: One people, parted by an old quarrel and not by kind
carrier: Sinnammu Mirpal, Yagrum Bagarn, topic Zenar
where_in_game: Ahemmusa camp; Corprusarium at Tel Fyr
note: Six informed voices answer the invented topic Zenar; nobody else does.

claim: The Zenad found a world nothing could live on and reworked it. They made nothing, and it spent them
carrier: Vivec, topic Dwemer's sin, appended to his own confession
where_in_game: main quest, Vivec, straight after the confession
note: Canon Part 4. Built from the document, so revising Part 4 and rebuilding is the whole edit.

claim: There is one Maker, and he cannot be seen for categorical reasons, not technical ones
note: Shared Part 7's delivery rule: once per game, one character, no framing. Constraint 6 drops the lead-in at revision.

claim: The trace: a passenger in every cell, older than the disease, in every living thing
where_in_game: Tel Fyr, once he has the player's blood on the glass - the main-quest cure
note: Canon Part 5. Never names the Zenad; the player joins it to Vivec's trace in the blood.

claim: The swarm's own word: nanites
source: Shared 11 (the word has one kind of source)
carrier: Rararyn Radarys, a Sleeper, topic Dagoth Ur
where_in_game: Balmora streets, while Dagoth Fovon lives and sleeperOn = 1
note: Word settled by Faig 2026-09-20. Said in delirium, not understood, not remembered once freed. Never predicated of Dagoth Ur.

claim: Rain's Hand is when men began to use magicka, not when magicka began, and someone measured the distance
carrier: one paragraph added to Ffoulke's astronomy tract
note: Plants the question so a later answer has somewhere to land. Skyrim's flag 1 asks whether the paragraph is final.

claim: The naming table: Zenar, Zenad, Zenaric, Zetic; Charge and Discharge
carrier: 32 rules over 190 Lua record-fields and 229 plugin record-fields
where_in_game: everywhere the game speaks in its own voice
note: The rename is itself a carrier: it is what the player reads all game.

claim: The interface is the device, so it speaks the device's words
carrier: game settings, spell, potion and effect names
note: 290 arcane words are still in the engine's own voice - Cast Cost, a magical shield, Mage, College of Destruction. Queue item 4 in CLAUDE.md.

claim: One technology, one structure, each school its own light
note: A partial visual conversion reads as a bug; that is why it is all 141.

claim: Zenaric manufacture looks manufactured
note: A vanilla-profile player gets the text and the particles, not the ceramic suit.

claim: The Tribunal knows, and lied
note: Nothing of ours is needed: the source material already has one founder recanting.

claim: Corprus is not a disease. It is Zenar nanites running a hostile payload Dagoth Ur wrote
note: Recasts the main quest from cure to shutdown, and no line in the game says it. Fyr's line says only 'Not the disease'.

claim: Azura is the analytical side of the installation; the Nerevarine prophecy is a forecast, not a revelation
note: The prophecy is the spine of this game, and Azura appears at the end of it.

claim: The Zenad retooled their whole swarm for the terraforming: that is why the loss is permanent and why they cannot leave
note: Vivec says they spent nearly everything; he does not say what they spent it on, or why it cannot be undone.

claim: A soul gem catches the population of machines a body hosts, at the moment the body stops
note: Morrowind ships soul gems, Azura's Star and an enchanting economy, and says nothing. Part 0 rule 2 bounds what may be said.

claim: Everyone needs a key to address the medium; the player's is issued by the Empire
note: The Silence ability keyed to a whitelist of equipped item IDs is designed and never built: nothing in mod/ mentions it.

claim: The Heart of Lorkhan is a reactor
note: Vanilla calls it a source of power, which is compatible but is not ours.

claim: The Dwemer did not invent their machines. They found Zenar hardware and reverse-engineered it
note: His reply says he heard the word from them; it does not say the machines are derivative. Morrowind Part 5 drafted a line that does, and it was never placed.

claim: Vampirism and lycanthropy are Zenar equipment running on the wrong organism
note: Both are in the game: vampirism in Morrowind, werewolves in Bloodmoon.

claim: Swarm and field are one medium; capacity and access never substitute for each other
note: Morrowind has only the controller route, so a carrier here would be one voice noticing that a key is needed at all.

claim: The elements are by-products of a finite list of terraforming jobs
note: A mage or a Telvanni is the obvious mouth; none is written.

claim: Racial differences in capacity are trace density and nothing else
note: The game ships the numbers - Altmer magicka, Breton resistance - and no explanation of ours.

claim: Meridia took an installation that was not hers
note: Morrowind has only her shrine. Listed so that the absence is a decision and not an oversight.
